Unsolicited observation 1, outside this round's assigned scope. In test_disallowed_methods_expect_sites, the test-file exception is a crate-level #![expect(clippy::disallowed_methods)] with a reason naming a process spawn. The only guard is that the file must not contain the token `ResolvedApiKey`. A crate-level expect also silences a ResolvedApiKey::as_str read made through an inferred type, for example a value returned from a function, because the file never names the type. Tightening: require item-level expects on the spawning helper in test files, or a named test-support module, so a crate-level expect cannot cover a secret read. Class would be boundary_tightening, minor.

Unsolicited observation 2, outside this round's assigned scope. The D0 outcome "counted, self entries rejected" bans every self dev-dependency. It conflates two cases. If cross-crate dev edges are counted but the self edge is ignored, self entries are stale and rejected, yet the self dev-dependency needs no entry. In that mixed case the branch forces the [[test]] required-features rework unnecessarily. Add a fourth line for "self edge ignored", or word the third branch as "self edge flagged and entry rejected". Class would be doc_gap, minor.
